subject: computer-science
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of cache memory in a CPU?
options: To hold frequently used data and instructions close to the CPU for fast access
To replace the need for RAM entirely
To increase the total amount of secondary storage
To store data permanently when the computer is switched off
questions.explain: Cache is small, very fast memory that stores frequently accessed data so the CPU does not have to wait for slower RAM.

questions.q: Which is a key advantage of a solid state drive (SSD) over a magnetic hard disk drive?
options: It has no moving parts, so it is faster and more durable
It is always cheaper per gigabyte
It always has a larger storage capacity
It is volatile and so loses data quickly
questions.explain: SSDs have no moving parts, making them faster and more shock-resistant than magnetic drives.

questions.q: How many bits are there in one byte?
questions.explain: One byte is made up of exactly 8 bits.

questions.q: Which is an example of utility software?
options: A word processor
A video game
A presentation tool
Disk defragmentation software
questions.explain: Defragmentation software is utility software that maintains and optimises the computer system.

questions.q: What is the correct order of the fetch-decode-execute cycle?
options: Execute, decode, fetch
Decode, fetch, execute
Fetch, decode, execute
Fetch, execute, decode
questions.explain: The CPU first fetches an instruction from memory, decodes what it means, then executes it.

questions.q: Increasing which of the following would most directly allow a CPU to execute more instructions per second?
options: The clock speed
The size of the hard drive
The number of USB ports
The resolution of the monitor
questions.explain: A higher clock speed means more fetch-decode-execute cycles are completed each second.

questions.q: Which list places units of storage in order from smallest to largest?
options: kB, byte, MB, GB
Byte, bit, MB, GB
Bit, byte, kB, MB
Byte, bit, GB, MB
questions.explain: A bit is the smallest unit, then a byte, then a kilobyte, then a megabyte.

questions.q: What is the role of the Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) in the CPU?
options: It permanently stores the operating system
It decodes instructions and manages the fetch-execute cycle
It carries out arithmetic calculations and logical operations
It connects the CPU to secondary storage
questions.explain: The ALU performs all arithmetic (such as addition) and logical (such as comparisons) operations.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a role of the operating system?
options: Managing files and the file system
Handling input and output devices
Managing memory and processes
Editing a customer's word-processed letter
questions.explain: Editing a document is done by application software; the operating system manages hardware, memory, files and processes.

A network of computers sharing files over the internet
A general-purpose computer that runs many different applications
A computer built into a larger device to perform a dedicated task
questions.explain: An embedded system is a computer dedicated to a specific function within a larger device, such as a washing machine controller.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes the von Neumann architecture?
options: The CPU has no need for any registers
Instructions and data are stored in physically separate memories
Programs are stored permanently in the ALU
Program instructions and data are stored in the same memory
questions.explain: In the von Neumann architecture a single shared memory holds both program instructions and the data they operate on.

questions.q: Which statement about ROM is correct?
options: It can be easily rewritten thousands of times during normal use
It is volatile and loses its contents when switched off
It is used as the computer's main working memory
It is non-volatile and typically holds the boot/start-up instructions
questions.explain: ROM is non-volatile and usually stores the start-up (boot) instructions the computer needs when first switched on.
